subject: tech
title: Parts of a Computer
about: The parts of a computer and the job each one does: the screen, keyboard, mouse and trackpad, touch screen, speaker, microphone, camera, headphones, battery and charger, the processor chip that works like a brain, the memory that keeps things, the printer and the cable. NC K2-CS-02 (describe what common hardware does, using the right words). Read it together with his tablet in front of you so he can touch each part as it comes up.
tip: Put his tablet in front of him and have him touch each part as the card names it: screen, camera, speaker, charger.

cards.q: Which part of a computer shows the pictures and words?
cards.note: The screen is also called a monitor. Everything the computer shows you appears there.

cards.q: You want to type your name. Which part do you use?
cards.note: A keyboard has a key for every letter and number. Press a key and that letter appears on the screen.

cards.q: You slide it on the desk and the pointer on the screen moves. What is it?
cards.note: A computer mouse has a tail-like cord or no cord at all. Slide it and the arrow on the screen slides too.

cards.q: On a laptop, what is the flat square you rub with a finger to move the pointer?
cards.note: A trackpad does the mouse's job on a laptop. Slide one finger to move and tap to click.

cards.q: On a tablet you tap the screen itself to make things happen. What kind of screen is that?
cards.note: A touch screen feels your finger. It shows pictures and takes your taps, both at once.

cards.q: Which part plays the music and sounds you hear?
cards.note: The speaker turns the computer's sound into sound for your ears. Turn it down when others are near.

cards.q: You talk to the tablet and it hears you. What catches your voice?
cards.note: A microphone catches your voice and sends it into the computer. It is tiny, often just a little hole.

cards.q: Which part lets the tablet take a photo or see your face?
cards.note: The camera is the little round eye on the front or back. It sees, but it does not hear.

cards.q: What do you wear on your ears so only you hear the sound?
cards.note: Headphones are little speakers for your ears. Keep the sound low so your ears stay healthy.

cards.q: A tablet works with no cord plugged in. What is storing the power inside?
cards.note: The battery holds electricity. When it runs low, the tablet needs its charger.

cards.q: The battery is almost empty. What does a grown-up plug in to fill it up?
cards.note: The charger fills the battery back up with electricity from the wall. A grown-up does the plugging in.

cards.q: Deep inside is a chip that works like a brain. What is its name?
cards.note: People call the processor the computer's brain. It follows the instructions, millions of steps every second.

cards.q: You save a drawing and it is still there tomorrow. What keeps it safe inside?
cards.note: Saved things live in the computer's storage. Many people call it the memory. It holds your pictures, games and words so they are there next time.

cards.q: Which machine puts your words and pictures onto paper?
cards.note: A printer puts ink onto paper in tiny dots. Out comes your drawing on a real page.

cards.q: What carries electricity from the wall to the computer?
cards.note: Cables carry electricity and information. Only a grown-up should plug things into the wall.

cards.q: What is another name for the computer screen?
cards.note: Monitor is a grown-up word for screen. Say mon-ih-ter.

cards.q: What is the little arrow on the screen that the mouse moves around?
cards.note: The pointer, also called the cursor, points at things. Move it onto a picture and click to pick it.
